interface.title: torchseed — graphical configuration builder for torchtree
interface.field: Phylogenetics / molecular evolution (Bayesian phylodynamics, molecular-clock time trees)
interface.stage_of_work: Analysis setup: preparing the data and specifying the model before running inference offline
interface.what_it_is_for: A step-by-step wizard that loads an alignment, tip dates and a starting tree, checks how clock-like the data are, and turns the chosen substitution, clock, tree-prior, prior and variational-inference (ADVI) settings into a torchtree JSON config file to download.

data.note: I uploaded alignment.fasta (DNA, 10 taxa × 48 sites; taxon9 is all N), dates.csv (taxon9_2021.90 has no date, so it gives 9 of 10 dated) and tree.nwk. The app has no built-in example. The alignment viewer loads msa.js from a CDN, and it did render here.

tree.general: Specify a complete Bayesian model of how sequences evolved over time, check it against the data, and export it as a file that an inference engine runs elsewhere
tree.specific: Build a torchtree JSON config (GTR + Weibull + invariant sites, strict clock, Skygrid coalescent tree prior with GMRF, ADVI) from a FASTA alignment, tip dates and a Newick tree, then download samples.json. Caveat: in this run the exported samples.json was generated while the dates came from dates.csv, so only 9/10 taxa were dated and taxon9 has no date attribute; the dates were reset to 10/10 only after export and the file was not regenerated

features.name: Sequence alignment import with type dialog and colour viewer
features.general: Upload a sequence file, say what kind of sequences it holds, see a one-line summary of samples × positions, and open a colour-coded grid of the whole alignment to spot bad samples
features.specific: FASTA upload → Import Options dialog (DNA/Protein) → table row (Name, File, Taxa, Sites, Type) with view and delete buttons → Alignment viewer modal (msa.js)
steps: Choose DNA or Protein in the Import Options dialog and press Import
Read the Taxa and Sites counts in the row
Press the eye button to open the colour-coded alignment viewer
Close it, or remove the alignment with the bin button
serves_tasks: Import a sequence dataset and confirm how many samples and positions it has
Look at the raw sequences to spot bad samples

features.name: Sample-date extraction from names or a table, with coverage check and histogram
features.general: Give every sample a decimal date, either by matching a pattern in its name or by joining a table, then see how many samples got a date, the date range, a per-sample age/height column whose meaning depends on the chosen time direction (age relative to the newest sample when counting forward from a past origin; the raw date was shown under 'before present'), and a histogram whose bin count you can change. The coverage count is the only warning that a sample is undated
features.specific: Dates tab: Use tip dates checkbox, Time direction, Date source radio (regex / CSV), 'Parse dates from taxon names', the 'Dates loaded for N/M taxa · range' banner, the Date table (Taxon, Date, Age/Height; CSV download), and a Date histogram with a bins slider
steps: Choose regex or CSV as the date source
Parse with the regex or upload the CSV
Read the N/M coverage banner and the date table
Open the histogram and drag the bins slider
serves_tasks: Attach a collection time to every sample so the analysis can be calibrated in real time
Check how the sampling times are spread
Redo the date assignment so that every sample is dated

features.name: Interactive tree viewer with layout switching
features.general: Draw a loaded tree in a pop-up window and change its layout, zoom and spacing to inspect its shape and labels
features.specific: '👁 View tree' modal with ＋/－ Zoom, Spacing ↕＋/↕−, a Layout select (Rectangular, Diagonal, Hierarchical, Radial, Circular) and Reset
steps: Upload a Newick or NEXUS tree
Switch the layout, e.g. to Circular
serves_tasks: Load a starting tree and look at it

features.name: Root-to-tip regression with best-root search
features.general: Test whether divergence grows linearly with sampling time: search for the root that best fits by a chosen criterion, then show the slope (rate), the x-intercept (origin date), r² and point count, with a scatter plot, fitted line and hover labels. Only dated samples are used, so check the point count against the number of samples
features.specific: Tree tab expander: 'Optimisation criterion' (r² or SSR) + Compute → metrics Rate (slope), TMRCA (x-intercept), r², n tips, and a Plotly plot of root-to-tip distance vs date
steps: Load a tree and assign dates
Read the rate, TMRCA, r² and n tips
Hover points to identify outlying samples
serves_tasks: Check that genetic divergence grows steadily with sampling time before assuming a clock
Choose how evolutionary rate varies across lineages and give it a starting value

features.name: Model picker with parameter table, estimate toggles and formula preview
features.general: Pick a model from a list and get its free parameters, each with a starting value and a fix-or-estimate switch, plus the model's formula drawn as maths
features.specific: Substitution model dropdown (JC69/HKY/GTR/K80/Custom) → rows like 'substmodel.frequencies' and 'substmodel.rates', each with a starting value and an Est. checkbox, and a rendered Q matrix and P(t)=e^{Qt}
steps: Tick or untick Est. for each parameter
serves_tasks: Choose how characters change along the tree and how rates vary between positions

features.name: Discretised rate-heterogeneity preview
features.general: Turn on rate variation across positions, set its shape and the number of categories, and see the density curve with category cut lines and a table of category probabilities, quantiles and rates that updates live; optionally add a share of invariant positions
features.specific: 'Discretised Weibull rate categories' checkbox → Number of categories and sitemodel.shape (with Est.) → 'Show Weibull distribution' expander (density plot plus Prob/Quantile/Rate table); '+I' checkbox → sitemodel.pinv
steps: Open 'Show Weibull distribution' and watch the curve and rates table update
serves_tasks: Choose how characters change along the tree and how rates vary between positions

features.name: Hierarchical prior editor with hyperparameter promotion
features.general: Each estimated parameter gets a card where you choose a prior distribution and its settings. Any setting can be promoted to a parameter of its own, which adds a new card for its prior; you can unlink it again or remove a prior
features.specific: Priors tab 'Parameter priors' cards (e.g. sitemodel.shape — [0,∞)): Distribution dropdown (Exponential, LogNormal, Normal, Gamma, Beta, Dirichlet, Laplace, …), '➕ add prior on <hyperparameter>' → 'linked to sitemodel.shape.exponential.rate' plus Unlink, a new card for that hyperparameter, and 🗑 Remove
steps: Choose a distribution and set its values
Press '➕ add prior on rate' to promote the hyperparameter
Edit the new card for the hyperparameter (e.g. switch it to Gamma)
serves_tasks: Set prior distributions on every estimated parameter, including priors on the priors' own settings

features.name: Tree-prior selector that adds the priors it needs
features.general: Choose a population-history model for the tree; the form shows that model's settings and adds the smoothing prior and hyperprior it requires
features.specific: Coalescent model dropdown (None / Constant / Exponential / Skyglide / Skygrid / Skyride); Skygrid shows Number of epochs and Cutoff time, sets coalescent.theta dim=10, and adds a GMRF prior on coalescent.theta.log with a Gamma prior on gmrf.precision
steps: Check the added GMRF and precision prior cards
serves_tasks: Choose a population model as the prior on the tree

features.name: Config generation with preview, summary and download
features.general: Build the final machine-readable analysis file from everything set in the earlier steps, browse it as a collapsible tree, list its components, and download it. It checks only that the required inputs are loaded, not that every sample is dated
features.specific: Output tab: refuses until an alignment and tree are loaded; then Generate / Refresh JSON → 'Configuration ready.' (shown even with undated taxa), a JSON preview expander, a Component summary (id, type) and 'Download samples.json' (file name taken from the output stem on the Algorithm tab)
steps: Load the required inputs (otherwise a notice appears)
serves_tasks: Generate the analysis file, check it, and save it

features.name: Variational-inference settings panel with per-parameter approximations
features.general: Lay out an approximate-inference run: how the tree's node heights are reparameterised, a variational location and scale for each estimated parameter together with the transform that maps it to its support, the optimiser with its learning rate and iteration count, the convergence test, and the output name and number of posterior samples
features.specific: Algorithm tab: node-height reparameterisation (Proportions, root-height offset), per-parameter variational loc/scale rows with their transforms, Adam optimiser (lr, iterations), Stan ELBO convergence (samples, frequency, tolerance), output stem and posterior sample count. Seen only; no value was edited in this run
steps: Read the node-height reparameterisation and root-height offset
Read each parameter's transform and variational loc/scale
Read the optimiser, learning rate and iterations
Read the ELBO convergence settings, output stem and number of samples
serves_tasks: Review the settings of the approximate-inference method
